correctness.rationale: Orthogonal three-vector Lanczos coordinates give A[v1 v2]=[v1 v2] [[alpha,a],[a,beta]]+b v3 e2^T. Writing Gram metric G=S^T S on this span, sketched Ritz H=G11^-1 G1: A:,1:2 has offdiagonals a+bt1, a and second diagonal beta+bt2, where t=G11^-1 G12. The eigenvalue discriminant is (alpha-beta-bt2)²+4a(a+bt1). For (1-epsilon)I<=G<=(1+epsilon)I, every 2D compression yields ||t||<=epsilon/sqrt(1-epsilon²); hence maximum imaginary part is bounded by sqrt([a(b epsilon/sqrt(1-epsilon²)-a)]_+). The sharp SPD 3x3 tridiagonal and Gram G=[[1-e²,0,-e sqrt(1-e²)],[0,1,0],[-e sqrt(1-e²),0,1+e²]] attain equality with eigenvalues 1±e,1, and become defective at epsilon=a/sqrt(a²+b²). Independent symbolic checks confirmed H, Gram spectrum, characteristic polynomial and critical threshold; the universal bound rests on the compression inequality.

final_claim: For the two-step sketched Rayleigh–Ritz compression of any real symmetric A with successive Lanczos links a>0,b>=0, a (1±epsilon) squared-norm embedding of the first two Lanczos vectors and the next residual guarantees real Ritz values when epsilon<=a/sqrt(a²+b²), and every eigenvalue imaginary part is bounded by sqrt([a(b epsilon/sqrt(1-epsilon²)-a)]_+). This deterministic bound is sharp over admissible systems/sketches, including SPD three-dimensional witnesses and a defective equality transition.
limitations: Exact real symmetric two-step Lanczos and sketch embedding on three-dimensional residual span.
Bounds are worst-case over admissible systems, not necessary for every fixed matrix or a multi-step convergence guarantee.
